utterances.text: But he's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's putting to the witness that he didn't meet with Sead Cirkin. It's clear in both the statement and the Stakic transcript that he did meet with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Stakic, but in the transcript which was admitted into evidence in this trial, if he said he met with Cirkin, there's no point of putting that on another transcript, but let us -- let us see what he said in 11446 on -- I've lost the number. 11461. Yes. It says -- why don't you read it so that the witness can answer the question. I see the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Q. Do you know Sead Cirkin? "A. I've heard about Sead Cirkin. He's an active military. As far as I know, earlier, when the Serbs took Prijedor militarily, he tried to organise a defence of Kozarac in Kozarac. I do not know where he got it but he managed to put together some weapons and some guys who tried to organise Kozarac defence." [Interpretation] So you knew that he was the commander of the Kozarac defence.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I only said I knew of him and heard of him. Whether there was anyone else, I'm not sure, but as far as I know, he was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you say here that you've heard about him, not that you knew him and met him.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: You can twist my words as much as you like and we can debate it as long as you want, but I'm telling you loud and clear that I went to see him. I saw him for five minutes and then I returned and had nothing more to do with him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this page be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he say here that he did not meet Mr. Cirkin? But in any event, we will admit this page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1923, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Merdzanic, you say that -- how long did the fighting for Kozarac last?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: From the 24th to the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of losses the Serb side took?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: How could I know? I suppose there were no great losses, because first they used tanks and artillery to shell Kozarac. The Muslims had nothing to open fire from against that. They only had regular infantry weapons. And then when Serbs moved with their infantry, I don't know. I was not at the front line. I was in my infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Stakic page 7732, that 65 ter that's been admitted, you said you believed there were no military installations anywhere near Kozarac. Do you know that Cirkin's unit actually had mortars?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then when the fighting stopped after two days, you say that you retreated with all the medical equipment and supplies, anything that remained at the hospital. You retreated to the edge of Kozarac, into the woods.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Not after two days. The very next day, on the 25th, in the morning. And not with all the medical supplies but only what could fit in one car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you went to some unfinished house where the police from Kozarac were already hiding; correct?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the hill or to Kurevo?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, it's the suburb, the outskirts of Kozarac when you go uphill. I believe it's not far from a mosque to the left of the road. It's still inside Kozarac only at the outskirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Earlier today, Mrs. Sutherland interpreted your earlier statements to the effect that you called Serbs on the radio to accept certain wounded people, and they laughed at you, saying, "We'll kill you, Balijas." Where did you get a radio station?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It was not a radio station. It was a police vehicle, and every police vehicle is fitted with a radio set to a certain frequency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the police enabled you to talk to the police, not to your colleagues, doctors.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, they were not doctors. I suppose it was someone in the army or whoever commanded that attack against Kozarac. At any rate, via that same radio, the surrender of Kozarac was agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we passed the time to take a break. If it is convenient, shall we take a break now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we -- I omitted mentioning to you, Ms. Sutherland, that with respect to the associate exhibits, the 65 ter 20760, which is another drawing depicted by the witness, lacks the English translation. So until then, pending the English translation, we'll mark it for identification. We'll take a break for 20 minutes and resume at 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know, Dr. Merdzanic, that certain groups went uphill and some went to the woods in Kurevo and reorganised the battle there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's just finish this. You talked from a police vehicle, so you were only able to speak to a policeman, not your colleagues at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was certainly not talking to colleagues at the hospital. Earlier, when the ultimatum expired, the Serbs cut off the telephones so you couldn't call Kozarac or from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But then you said the next day an ambulance came, and that the most seriously injured were taken to the hospital in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I said on the 26th, when the surrender of Kozarac had been negotiated, conditions were agreed with the police how to carry out this surrender. And then in a convoy, the wounded, the police, and the civilians came out, but the police were then separated from the rest and they were killed, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that, Dr. Merdzanic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that. I was in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying the Serb policemen killed the Muslim policemen then and there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it was the police who killed them. When they went into Kozarac, it was not policemen. It was uniformed troops with military tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This first, 1D04456, page 8. You gave the federal police in Keln [phoen] an interview saying that one of the next days an ambulance arrived and took away the more seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No. I have my exact statement with the description how it happened. I can repeat it. The surrender was agreed. No ambulance arrived. We had an ambulance, and one of our drivers, the husband of Azra Blazevic, got into that ambulance and carried away the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: As had been agreed. They drove towards the road from Prijedor to Banja Luka, and then I believe they took the right-hand to Prijedor. We didn't accompany them. We remained in Kozarac, and we went back to the ambulance -- to the infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the time the hospital was held by the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It was in Serb hands always.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that, throughout the war, hundreds and thousands of Muslims and Croats were given treatment in that same hospital?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: During the war, hundreds of thousands of Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I say hundreds and maybe thousands of Muslims and Croats received dialysis and were given complete medical assistance.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. You have to ask in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have this information. I'm just asking you as a doctor. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was in Kozarac. How would I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the civilians from Kozarac, just before the attack and during the attack, were called and came to Prijedor and found shelter in Muslim and Serbian houses while the fighting lasted?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I know that on the 22nd, when the ultimatum expired, they said nobody would be able to get in or out anymore, and by the 24th, two women came to the infirmary. They were about to give birth, and they said that they could not go to Prijedor, and I had to deliver them, with a nurse -- with a midwife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D04461, in the Brdjanin case, page 11801, you said there were problems with civilians who did not know that Kozarac had surrendered.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Well, the telephones were not working, and those who did not hear the announcement that everyone was supposed to get out remained in their homes. And, of course, the Serbs who came in, I know of one woman whose name was Sahuric who was in a basement with other civilians and later came to Trnopolje looking for somebody who would be able to bury those civilians, because the Serbs found them in that basement in Kozarac and killed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who can confirm that story, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That woman, Sahuric, if she's still alive. They live in Germany. She has a son. I gave once the Office of the Prosecutor their names and telephone number. Whether they had contacted them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Brdjanin, you also say, on page 11801, lines 18 to 21, that there was a young wounded boy and a wounded Serb who were allowed to go to Prijedor, and then you say you heard the policemen were killed on the spot. Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I heard that later in Trnopolje from people who were there, who got out of them [as interpreted] on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who told you that by name?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you came to Trnopolje on the 26th of May. You were ordered to bring all your medical equipment, all you doctors, and there you set up medical protection for the people in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. That's completely wrong. I don't know where -- how you come up with that. When we were arrested in Kozarac at the infirmary, three soldiers came in. Dragan Skrbic was one of them. You can ask him. He's still alive. They ordered us first to wait while they decide what to do with us. Then they brought a military truck. We had to put all our medical supplies and equipment onto that military truck, and it was all driven away. I don't know where. None of it, not a single item of all that, ever arrived at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP, dated 27 and 28 August, 2000, that's 1D04457, page 01035295, you said that medical equipment was loaded and taken to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's do it one by one. Let's upload that statement, 1D4457. Could you repeat the page? Here it is. Thank you. Ending with 5295.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 95, 295, at the very end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 6. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can barely see it myself. Can it be zoomed in a bit? We should have the exact line too. Just a moment, please. Eighteen through 21.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. "Then the truck left, and I never saw it again." I found it just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you have an indication of line numbers, it should be a transcript instead of statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. We're on the statement now. I cannot see that particular line in the statement, though. It is this page, 295.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you help us, Doctor? Where is that?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It was here in the Bosnian language a moment ago, but now somebody removed all of it. Stop. Stop. That's it. Here at the bottom. It says: "Then the truck left --" well, once again what is this? Can I see the entire line, please? Fine. Just leave it this way, please. You don't need to do anything else. Thank you. So look at the bottom down here. "Then the truck left. I don't know where it went, but I never saw the supplies again." I really don't see where you get this from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at the entire paragraph.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Just go ahead and have a look at the entire paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what was it that you took to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: As for medical supplies, we didn't take any of that to Trnopolje. As a matter of fact, I didn't even manage to take my rucksack. Azra managed to take a few things in her rucksack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But just personal belongings, no military -- or, rather, medical material, no, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But before that sentence the witness read earlier on, it reads: "We loaded all of the medical supplies we had from the clinic on this truck. " Are you referring to this sentence, Mr. Karadzic? Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's on transcript page 7740 and 7741 of the Stakic transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Not Trnopolje. I mean the fact -- how the witness has answered at lines 18 to 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, tell us, you arrived in Trnopolje, and you say that uniformed persons came to get you. What kind of uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Again, completely erroneous. You have to have a clear idea as to how all of this happened. We were taken prisoner in Kozarac. We were taken to the centre of Kozarac. Nihad Bahonjic was taken out there and we heard later on that he had been killed. Then they took us in a military jeep in the direction of Prijedor to a tavern on the left-hand side. Then they ordered us to board a bus that was coming from Prijedor. There were women and children on that bus with a military escort, and that's the bus that we arrived in at Trnopolje. When we got off the bus in Trnopolje, there were very many men in uniform. One of them was Rade Baltic in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. When they came to get you, Predrag Behic, whatever his name is, Dragan Skrbic, and another one, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: They wore camouflage military uniforms. One of them had a red beret, and all of them had on their upper arm a particular emblem. I cannot remember the colour. I think that Skrbic even wore a blue camouflage uniform whereas the others had green camouflage uniforms. Most of the men we saw in Kozarac as we walked to the centre wore camouflage military uniforms and they all had these armbands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is a band made of cloth, right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes, some kind of cloth, linen probably. So that they could be able to tell them apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that there was a radio broadcast saying that all the civilians who did not wish to fight should wear such an armband and that all houses from which there would be no shooting should be marked with a white cloth?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't understand how you think that the people of Kozarac can hear that. You cut off electricity, telephones, everything else. How do you expect people to hear that information or broadcast? I've never heard of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That will do, the fact that you did not hear it. It's not only Kozarac. There are other parts of Prijedor as well.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, there are other parts, and you also shelled them and killed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, let us leave all these general things aside. You say that some unknown Serb wanted to kill you but that Skrbic forbade him to do that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, it's not exactly the way it was. He was just very nervous, and he was saying they should be all killed. It's not that Skrbic got up, and it's not that this man really tried to kill us and that Skrbic got up and stopped him in that way. It was a bit different. Goga, who was a Serb woman, was with us and on her white coat she had her name written --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us just see what you say here --

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am not interested in Goga, please. Did Skrbic stand in front of him and stop him from doing that, forbid that?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No. If you allow me, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us call up a text. Your statement given to the police in Kiel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D04456, page 9. 1D04456. Page 9. I'm going to read it out in English now so that the interpretation is better. I mean, so that they would do a better job than I would. "[In English] The Serb whose name I did not know wanted to kill us all immediately. However, Skrbic stood in front of us and forbade him to do it. He might have done this because he knew our veterinarian, Azra Blazevic, and had talked to our Serbian assistant before."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're guessing the reason why, but this is what you stated; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I can't really remember anymore, but I can tell you what my recollection is right now. This Serb was nervous, and he was saying that we should all be killed, and this Skrbic in some way prevented that, but not by standing in front of his rifle and protecting us that way with his own body. They called this Goga, this Serb, and talked to her separately, probably asking her what our role was during the shelling, and then he said that we should be left alone and that he would decide what would happen to us, and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Bahonjic was singled out. Do you know how many Bahonjics there were in the organisation of this struggle?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I know that Nihad Bahonjic is an ambulance driver and that from the beginning until the end, from the 24th until the 26th, he was at the infirmary with us and he did not take part in any of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you then say that you heard that he had been singled out and then you heard gunshots but you did not see him killed; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, but as far as I know, his bones have been found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with that later. So you heard this and you did not see it. All right. Now, tell me, in Trnopolje -- you were in Trnopolje; right? And, actually, when was this school built in Trnopolje, the municipal building, the infirmary, the stadium, the club, and also this warehouse for construction material?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: How could I know? At any rate, it was there for years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you said that in your opinion that was planned considerably earlier as a camp, because there is a railway -- railroad there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So when was that, 30 or 40 years before that, with the intention of having a camp there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's not true. That is not what I said. I said that strategically, if you look at Prijedor and the surrounding area, the only ideal spot for the Serbs where they could operate -- well, in principle, that camp had been prepared for ethnic cleansing, so when women and children are brought together there and when they are expelled from their houses and villages and when a sufficient number of civilians are gathered there, then a convoy is organised for expelling these civilians from Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were saying that now, and you said that in the Brdjanin case. You said in the Stakic case, though, that you thought that all of this was decided in haste; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think that's the way it was. It depends on the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that in Stakic, 65 ter 22147, on page 7827, but you said it could have been this way and it could have been that way; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was not involved in the decision-making. Ask someone who was involved in the decision-making as to where the camp would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that your impression was that both was plausible, that it was done in haste and that it could have been done earlier.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I said that that was my impression. You have to ask whoever had planned that. However, if you look at where Trnopolje is and what Trnopolje was used for, there is not a better spot in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on, you say that before the war this spot had been fenced off; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Well, this was a small fence, a school fence, and also for the infirmary, the construction material warehouse. In principle, there was nothing new that was built there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at a video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The quality of the image is very poor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 40504. That's the 65 ter number. And then 24:00.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the fence, the low fence that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is a low fence. That was Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this fence is between what?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: You have to play the video further. That fence had to be between the house and the construction equipment store facing the football stadium, because that is the only fence that was that low -- that low.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. And that is where this warehouse with the construction material was fenced off?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, that's not right. That's a different fence, about 2 or 2.5 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was this fence used for?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That fence had been prepared for the inmates from Keraterm. It was built just before the journalists arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How high is this fence?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: On that side it was perhaps 1.20 metres. I didn't measure it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play this on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you stop at this point, please? This is not that fence. This is somewhere near the school. This is the other fence, the normal fence that was filmed later on when the Serb journalists came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Actually, that was the fence surrounding the school; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I think so. On the Penny Marshall footage that can be seen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Reporter: That means practically that the fence does not separate you from the village. "Prisoner: No, no, they let us go out. We leave our personal identity card here and go up there. "Prisoner: But there's no one in the village. We just go into the gardens and get the vegetables. "Reporter: That means you are free to take a hoe and dig up something in the garden, right? "Prisoner: Yes, we take a hoe, go up there, dig up potatoes, tomatoes. We cook here for ourselves. "Second prisoner: It's all running out. "Prisoner: A few more days and there won't be anything up there left either."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you spoke about that. I'll tell you where now. You told about that in your interview from 2000, 1D04457, on page 296. It ends with number 296. You said it was the normal fence surrounding the schoolhouse from back before the war. There was one fence around the depot of construction materials.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another fence was around the school.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a third fence?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Outside the infirmary, a low fence next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: And the fence that was put up before the journalists arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the arrival of the reporters a fence was put up for the journalists?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No. It was for the inmates of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And there was a section without any fence whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The section closer to the football pitch. There was no fence there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D4851.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe this footage -- this aerial photograph is familiar to you. Can you see the football pitch here to the left?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can see the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There was no fence on that side. And what is the rest? Can you please explain?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: In the upper part we see the schoolhouse. Then you see the infirmary. Then this big hall, and close to the intersection is the shop selling construction material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is not part of an exhibit already, I would like to tender it. May I just ask you to mark --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. But before that are you minded to tender the previous video-clip we saw?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be first admitted. Ms. Sutherland, do you have any observation to that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Was that a question to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I asked Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the video is -- was an associated exhibit with Mr. Vulliamy, but I don't know about that particular portion that was -- that was played, whether that excerpt came in as an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you confirm it tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll wait. Then in relation to this document, but please tell us, Mr. Karadzic, first where this -- this document is from, whose marking this is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this witness marked it in another trial, Brdjanin or Stakic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember marking anything on an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the best we could find. We found it at the Tribunal. Could we ask the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you help us? At the end of this document it says P1770.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That was exhibit in the Stanisic/Zupljanin trial, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And do you know whose marking this is?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we ask the usher to help Dr. Merdzanic to make his own markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'm sorry. It was marked by this witness in the Stanisic/Zupljanin case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When was it? Do you remember when it was, the date of his testimony?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 9th of December, 2010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Last year. Doctor, do you remember now, having been assisted by the Prosecutor? Do you confirm that's your marking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. It's not a problem. This is Trnopolje for sure, and I can mark everything I recognise and I know here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question was whether you can recognise your markings. These markings were done by you -- by you yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's -- we'll -- our usher will assist you to add some further markings, probably black -- in black this time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In another colour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, by the school building, please put number 1. You may do it even outside the red line. Could you mark the side closer to the stadium with 2.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that's the side where there was no fence; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: There was no fence on that side. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, inside, can you identify the infirmary as 3?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the warehouse of construction material with 4. There was a fence around it; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there another building you think needs marking?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I'll put 5 to mark this cultural hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the cultural hall.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: There was a library in the community hall. At one point between the warehouse and -- of construction material and that community hall a fence was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you put the date at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1924, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: About the arrival at Trnopolje, you said there was no registration of newly arrived.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Not that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Still, you did give Slavko Puhalic a certain list, and you were told that it was necessary in case somebody went missing.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Only of those who were in the infirmary. Those who were going to the school and the community hall were not listed that I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You spoke about people being able to go out, and we heard on this footage that people went out into the village to find food and came back.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Not exactly. There were several periods during the existence of Trnopolje, and during various periods, food supplies were organised in a different way. There was one stage when the surrounding population had been expelled and sent away in a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. We heard this man on the video saying that nobody beat him, that he had not been involved in combat, that he had come there to find shelter, and that they were able to go out. He said, "We could take a hoe, go into the gardens, dig out vegetables," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Play the video where they interviewed me, I didn’t say anything either. They went into the infirmary, too. It was a Serbian television crew. Do you think anybody dared say anything openly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's look at it again. The interpreters have the text. We can continue where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you play, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Prisoner: They let us go out into the village. We go there alone. "Reporter: That means you're free to take a hoe and dig up something in the gardens; right? "Prisoner: Yes. We take a hoe, go up there, dig up potatoes, tomatoes. We cook here for ourselves. "Second prisoner: It's all running out, however. "Reporter: When did you come here? "Prisoner: On the 27th of May. "Reporter: And why did you come? "Prisoner: I came here when the fighting started where I lived. I had to come. Where would I go on the other side? "Reporter: Did you participate in combat? "Prisoner: No. "Reporter: So practically you were looking for protection, right? For safety? "Prisoner: Yes. "Reporter: And what is it like here? "Prisoner: Well, you can see for yourself it's okay. It's not so bad. "Reporter: Were there any problems, any mistreatment? "Prisoner: No. "Reporter: What about the others, anyone else here, because I saw here that the -- in the camp we visited a little while ago, people from another collection centre had arrived, and did this collection centre function like some kind of camp where people were mistreated? "Prisoner: Well, this is a collection centre. Fuck it. It cannot be anything other than a collection centre. All those who didn't fight came here. What do I have to fight for? "Reporter: And what now? "Prisoner: Only those who were being shelled had to come here. "Reporter: And what do you expect now? If only those big guys --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not finish.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can just add it to the previous footage admitted. We don't have to give it a separate exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you hear what he said? There was fighting in surrounding villages. There was shooting. They came here. They were looking for food. Did you hear anyone asking him --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic has to slow down. We cannot catch up with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Merdzanic. We have to start it over again. Because of the overlap the interpreters were not able to catch up with you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Merdzanic, did this man say that there was shooting or shelling there, that he was not involved in combat, that he came there, and they are making do to find food, going out into surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was in that village from beginning to end --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to answer now and please don't interrupt me. I was in that camp from beginning to end, and I know exactly in what way people came and how things were done in various periods. There were various distinct periods in Trnopolje, and in different periods the inmates received different treatment. Speaking of most of the inmates, and I never said that all of them were beaten or killed, but many were beaten and some were even killed in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, it's a different subject. We'll come to it. I want to finish with this subject.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain to you that what this young man is saying to the Serbian television crew -- you either have to say what he is saying or you say nothing. Just find this man and bring him here. Let's see what he's going to say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that he says that the guards were trying to help the Muslims and the Serbs from the surrounding villages also came and tried to help with what they had?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: On that subject, I just said that there were certain Serbs who tried to be helpful to us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I don't know -- I know this has been exhibited already, and my assistants will provide the exact minutes of -- of this segment. It belongs with the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The additional part that we just saw will be added to the previous exhibit -- Exhibit D1924. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was mistaken. The OTP will confirm later on whether this is a part that we already admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that is the right segment. I don't think this segment has been exhibited, not this part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That being the case with -- this part will be added to the existing video-clip. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in Brdjanin, 1D04458, page 11813, lines 4 through 7, you said that the guards tried to be helpful and did what they could, at least some of them, but there were also Serbs who visited and tried to help; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I never said Serbs were all bad or all Serbs were bad. I said, indeed, that there were certain Serbs who visited and tried to help us as much as they could. I also said there was one period, but it was only a short period, where inmates were allowed under escort to go to surrounding farms and bring potatoes and whatever food they found in empty houses because there was no other food available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You spoke about intermittent arrivals from Keraterm and Omarska. How often did groups come, and how large were there -- they?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: From Keraterm there was only one group. And from Omarska, a group of women came with minor children, and as far as I know, after the journalists left, a larger group came that night after the journalists left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That means there was one group from Keraterm and how many from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Two groups. One was women and underage children, and the other time those from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that 59 were -- per cent were released from Omarska and 41 per cent were sent to Manjaca? Just tell me if you know that or not.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they came from Trnopolje -- they came to Trnopolje, and most of them were released from Trnopolje, because, for instance, my wife's father, who with his own wife and her sister stayed at his home later, they were all found there and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- did you say it was agreed that local residents could visit and bring food to the camps?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was in the early days, when the population in the surrounding villages were still there in their homes, before they were driven out of their homes and expelled in convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Of course I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were in Elezi when that happened?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No, no. This was right by Trnopolje. People were brought to Trnopolje. Not only from Elezi but also from other areas. The ethnic cleansing of Prijedor was complete. Most of it happened through Trnopolje, not all of it though. One convoy from Sanski Most, as a matter of fact, was brought to Trnopolje. They were boarded onto a train. They took a man and a woman out --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, I don't have time for your very general statements, and I have no time to make them more specific. You did complain about Zoran Zigic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic? I didn't complain. I just gave a statement saying that on one occasion, Zoran Zigic came to Trnopolje. After they brought the inmates from Keraterm, he lined them up within that fence that had been built for them. He brought out one of them named Kum and told him to kneel down and then he beat him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that several criminal reports were filed against him?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that, but I know that the commander of the guards and the commander of the company were all there. Everybody was watching. It was out in the open. No one reacted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, interpreters didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I asked whether Dr. Merdzanic knew that he had been a criminal and that criminal reports had been filed against him.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I've already responded that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably what the interpreters missed was the exhibit number, the document number that we are -- in front of us and that we are seeing now, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a translation too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is one criminal report dated the 2nd of July, because some -- actually, he had asked some Muslims for money, and obviously he was involved in a trade that was based on their fear.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It wasn't only him. When you expel the population from one village, then you start looting in the houses. When the houses are looted, it is only then that they are destroyed and razed to the ground. It is not that the Serbs move into these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see who it was that filed this criminal report. Simo Drljaca filed this criminal report; right? The chief of the station.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't know who filed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is, I take it, 1D4465. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1925, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4467. Can we have a look at that now. 1D4467.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the version in our language. The translation is coming. Do you agree that the same chief of the police station is asking for Zoran Zigic to be taken to prison according to a decision such and such number and so on?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is just a piece of paper saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1926, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you never saw women being questioned; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's what I said in relation to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, you were never beaten; right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was not beaten. I just went and gave a statement on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Apart from that one statement, you were not interrogated.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you tell them then about all the things that you did in Kozarac during the crisis?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I always said the same thing that I've been saying now. There was this Serb woman, Goga. She made a statement too. Nothing else can be said except for what had truly happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your estimate was that about 10 per cent of these people who were there were taken out for questioning and were beaten.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have a look at this. I don't know what the context was possibly. I have to see the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D4457, your interview with the OTP. 0103502 [as interpreted] and 03. Those are the pages.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I said something like that, but I don't know whether that's the context. I'd have to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the same page, 04 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, what is this? 318? And we need 302 and 303. I don't know how this happened. 5302 and 03. Actually the numbers are the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not page 14 -- 14 in English, or 13.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thirteen, possibly, 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Zigic here, and you see that they were prosecuting him. And now let us see where you mentioned this percentage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's between pages 302 and 303. Can we have the next page, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I see the time. We'll continue tomorrow morning. We have to rise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, may I ask for a bit more time, because this is a man who was in Trnopolje, and unfortunately, there are quite a few general statements here, so I have to make them more specific. I have to get to the things that he does know specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You still have half an hour, which in the opinion the Chamber is sufficient for you to conclude. But we will see tomorrow. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning, but in the meantime, Dr. Merdzanic, as you are aware of this well, you are not supposed to discuss with anybody else about your testimony. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of November, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.00 p.m.,
